explanation:
別 combines the upper-body bone shape 冎 with a knife, 刀, now written as 刂 at the right. The action is separating the bones at their joints. It is a concrete form of dismembering or taking an articulated structure apart.

From this come dividing, separating, loosening connections, and parting. A separation also establishes a distinction, giving the senses of something different or of considering things separately.

The related 分 and 半 concern division into portions, while 辨 concerns distinguishing. 別 shares this wider vocabulary but retains the particular image of a knife working between bones. The compact modern left side preserves that earlier skeletal outline.
